text:
ashley: Ran a RoPE-scale modulation sweep across Llama-2-13B, Mixtral-8B, and Qwen-7B comparing linear / NTK / YARN variants. Short summary: Mixtral-8B with NTK scaling shows a sharp perplexity cliff around scale=1.8 and a coincident latency regression via kernel fallback.

matt: can you paste the exact command and config you used for the sweep?

ashley: ran on ded-rt-03. command snippet: 
```
./run_rope_sweep --model=mixtral-8b --variant=ntk --scale_min=0.8 --scale_max=2.2 --steps=15 \\
  --kv_policy=sticky --batcher=continuous --kernel_pref=fused,matmul --seed=42
```
observed behavior: baseline ppl ~12.4 until ~1.78, then jumps to ~23.5 at 1.82. profiler shows a kernel selector transition at that scale.

sara: do you have the runtime logs showing a kernel change or was it just a different perf path? paste log snippet.

ashley: log excerpt: 
```
[12:01:22] kernel_select: chosen=fused_attn (perf_est=3.1ms)
[12:01:23] kernel_select: perf_est increased -> fallback=matmul_attn (perf_est=5.6ms)
[12:01:23] kv_cache: prefix_hits=0.88 evictions=0.02
[12:01:23] batcher: active_batch_size=4 -> 12
```

liam: eyeballing this: batcher increased packing and kernel selector moved to matmul. My hypothesis: higher RoPE scale increases per-token activation sizing/working set -> the adaptive batcher packs more requests -> working set grows and pushes fused kernel into register spill territory, which causes selector to prefer matmul.

matt: can we reproduce this in the perf harness with deterministic microbatching so we can isolate kernel selection from batcher effects?

ashley: yes. I ran a control with `--batcher=fixed:1 --kv_policy=evict_early` to keep single-request batches and limit kv growth. Results: ppl stayed near baseline (12.6 -> 13.1) across scale up to 2.0, latency per token stable. So packing appears necessary for the cliff.

sara: that supports an interaction: RoPE scaling -> per-token activation size increase -> more KV memory per request -> adaptive batcher increases batch packing -> register pressure spikes -> kernel fallback -> perf cliff and quality regressions.

liam: model-specific detail: Mixtral uses head_kv_dim=64 whereas Llama and Qwen use 128. Smaller head/kv dims mean the threshold of register pressure is closer, so working-set increases more quickly push fused kernel into spill. Qwen didn't manifest the cliff (head_kv_dim=128 and a weaker rotary base in this build).

matt: do we have perf counters showing register spill / shared mem usage correlating with fused->matmul transition?

ashley: yes—perf flame excerpt: 
```
fused_attn_kernel: sm_util=78% reg_spill=12%  (normal)
when scale>1.75 -> reg_spill climbs to ~40% -> throughput collapses
```

sara: sounds like our kernel selector relies too much on a coarse perf_est. We should surface a reg_spill estimate into the selector and prefer kernels with better register behavior when spill crosses a threshold.

liam: short-term mitigation: add a kv_pressure signal to the batcher so it limits batch packing when kv evictions / prefetch rates indicate high memory pressure. That will reduce the chance of flipping kernels mid-rollout.

matt: next steps / action items:
- ashley: produce a deterministic harness run for Mixtral-8B NTK at scales [1.6, 1.7, 1.8, 1.9] capturing per-token perf counters and reg_spill (harness run id: 1765432220).
- sara: draft change to kernel selector to include reg_spill penalty term in perf ranking (PR draft #3124).
- liam: prototype batcher kv_pressure cap and run A/B on a dedicated pool.

ashley: quick measurements from the deterministic harness:
- scale=1.7: ppl=13.1 latency=3.05ms reg_spill=14%
- scale=1.8: ppl=22.9 latency=6.2ms reg_spill=39%
- scale=1.9: ppl=25.1 latency=8.0ms reg_spill=51%
(these match the dev harness replication)

matt: I reproduced on a second machine. This is reproducible and causes long-context quality regressions. Please file a ticket.

sara: filed INF-1427 with reproduction steps, perf traces, and logs attached.

liam: interim workaround: add a per-model safe_scale upper bound in the model catalog for Mixtral-8B-NTK (cap=1.7). Also add a console notice explaining that exceeding the cap can trigger kernel fallback and degrade quality. Long-term: selector + batcher fixes.

ashley: I'll run the same YARN-variant sweep tomorrow over Llama-2-13B and Qwen-7B to map per-model safe ranges and confirm if YARN behaves differently vs NTK/linear.

matt: agree on catalog cap. Also add an alert to the console when a serving node encounters repeated kernel flip events for a model so SRE/SEs can triage.

build-bot: deploy pipeline started: batcher-kv-pressure-experiment pipeline id=2026-03-18-09

liam: I've allocated ded-rt-03 for 2 hours for deep profiling. Ping me for GPU access.

ashley: thanks all — I'll post final sweep summary, perf traces, harness ids, and PR links when available.
